title: NIST/NBS NSRDS 36 codebook crosswalk

source.citation: Mukerjee, P.; Mysels, K. J. Critical Micelle Concentrations of Aqueous Surfactant Systems. NBS NSRDS 36 (1971). DOI: 10.6028/NBS.NSRDS.36

scope: Maps original NIST/NBS legends to fields in the openly licensed PSDI export. It does not re-transcribe or validate all 4,990 individual records.

concentrationUnits.A: moles per 100 moles of solvent, including additives
concentrationUnits.C: moles per 100 moles of surfactant mixture
concentrationUnits.D: weight/volume percent (grams per 100 milliliters of solution)
concentrationUnits.E: percent saturation of solution by additive
concentrationUnits.P: weight/weight percent (grams per 100 grams of solution)
concentrationUnits.T: grams per 100 grams of surfactant mixture
concentrationUnits.U: moles per liter or kilogram of solution, unspecified

evaluation.1: Independently confirmed by at least two good-quality laboratories; high confidence, approximately within 1.5% for the same measurement approach, with method-to-method differences possible.
evaluation.2: Same apparent quality as category 1 but lacks independent confirmation.
evaluation.3: Selected: lower accuracy than categories 1 and 2, but the source considers it probably within 10% under the same approach.
evaluation.D: Disputed: conflicting values; the source says one may be correct but does not identify which.
evaluation.L: Literature listing for completeness; insufficient information to certify reliability.
evaluation.P: Preferred among differing reported values, but not rated in the selected or recommended categories.
evaluation.R: Reference to a literature value not tabulated in the dataset; may also signal duplicates or errors.
evaluation.X: Cross-reference for mixed surfactant systems tabulated under another compound number.

qualityRatings.description: The first character of the NIST two-character quality field describes material; the second describes measurement method. The authors caution that their subjective ratings can vary by about one category.

material.A: Highest purity, unlikely to be significantly improved.
material.B: Very pure; may contain significant traces of impurities.
material.C: Purified; likely to contain significant impurities.
material.D: Purified without special precautions against surfactant impurities.
material.G: Not purified; likely systematic errors of uncertain absolute and relative magnitude.
material.P: High purity claimed without supporting data.

method.G: Likely systematic errors of uncertain absolute and relative magnitude.

sourceSymbols.A: Misprint corrected in a figure quoted in the reference.
sourceSymbols.C: Units converted from a tabulation in the reference.
sourceSymbols.E: From equations in the reference of method results.
sourceSymbols.G: From a graph of CMC values in the reference.
sourceSymbols.K: From a graph of method results in the reference.
sourceSymbols.L: Also from personal communications with the author.
sourceSymbols.M: Units converted from the preceding value; this is a derived conversion, not an independent laboratory measurement.
sourceSymbols.P: From the NIST authors' plot of data in the reference.
sourceSymbols.T: Tabulated or figure quoted in the reference.

referenceScheme.codeFormat: The first two digits of a reference number encode publication year; the reference index lists the full citation. The author field uses first four letters of one or two authors.
referenceScheme.importantCaveat: The five-digit code is an index key, not a DOI. Preserve it as supplied and resolve it against the reference index; do not infer a full citation from the year prefix alone.
referenceScheme.unmatchedReferenceReview: See reference-code-review.csv. Code 58017 is present in the original index despite a leading OCR artifact. Code 63021 is absent from the printed index but its DONB/JAN citation is independently resolved via PubMed (PMID 14134118; DOI 10.1111/j.2042-7158.1963.tb12887.x); article measurement data were not ingested. Three rows remain unresolved: 45005 (2) and 69016 (1).

originalFieldNotes.CMC: May contain source text or status strings such as VALUES FROM REF IN CMC, GRAPH DATA NOT RETRIEVED, SUMMARIZING EQN ONLY, or QUESTIONABLE CRITERION; these are not numeric measurements.
originalFieldNotes.CMC Value 1-3 / CMC Units 1-3: Can contain source-reported and derived values. Consult the associated Source symbol; preserve values and units without silently merging them.
Two quality-rating letters as defined above.
originalFieldNotes.Method: Experimental-method description; NIST discusses method classes on printed pp. 8-11.

externalCitationResolution.citation: Donbrow M, Jan ZA. Refractometric Determination of the Critical Micelle Concentration of Non-Ionic Surface-Active Agents. J Pharm Pharmacol. 1963;15:825-830.
externalCitationResolution.scope: Bibliographic metadata only; article measurement data not ingested and reuse license not assessed.

curationDecision: The original legend now decodes units, source symbols, evaluation grades, quality ratings, and reference-code format. Of 4,973 numeric reference codes, 4,964 match the NIST index and six code-63021 rows have an independently resolved citation (metadata only); three rows remain unresolved (45005 x2, 69016 x1). Irregular/missing fields and 719 structure/name joins remain subject to review. Compound 2 has a documented NIST-name versus PSDI LLM-structure conflict. No source data values, units, or structures were changed.
